approved: Higher Education Support Amendment (Savings and Other Measures) Bill 2013
Higher Education Support Amendment (Savings and Other Measures) Bill 2013 - Second Reading - Read a second time

Defended the Higher Education Support Amendment (Savings and Other Measures) Bill 2013 as implementing Labor's own previously announced cuts, noted most self-education tax deduction claims come from people earning under $80,000 a year, and said Queensland Labor governments closed 139 schools over about 20 years compared with the current LNP government's plan to close only 6 while building 28 new schools.

Opposed the Higher Education Support Amendment (Savings and Other Measures) Bill, which imposes a 2 per cent efficiency dividend on universities in 2014 and 1.25 per cent in 2015 while scrapping the 10 per cent up-front fee discount, noting university graduates contribute $170 billion a year in wages to the economy.

Reported that Bendigo's BRIT TAFE announced 47 more redundancies, on top of 100 last year, and closed its school of mines after more than 150 years and its cabinetmaking course, citing this as a warning about the Higher Education Support Amendment (Savings and Other Measures) Bill 2013's funding cuts.

Defended the Higher Education Support Amendment (Savings and Other Measures) Bill 2013 as implementing Labor's own savings measures announced on 13 April, while announcing the government would reverse Labor's $2,000 annual cap on tax deductions for self-education expenses, and accused Labor of hypocrisy for opposing cuts it originally proposed.
